statement: For a hyperbolic curve over a finite extension F of Q(mu_infty), abelianized point sections are equal only for the same point in positive genus; in genus zero, distinct x,y have equal classes exactly when the boundary is F-split and every h(a)/h(b), h(t)=(t-x)/(t-y), is a root of unity.
depends_on: A1; generalized Abel-Jacobi and Kummer comparison proved here
notes: Includes the exact parametrization on U03 and proves that a nonsplit boundary cannot produce a distinct equal-class pair. Equality is in the geometric abelian quotient, with its comparison map specified.

statement: The full point-section map is injective for every hyperbolic curve over F, every finite extension of F, and every finitely generated extension of F.
depends_on: D1; A1; AE1; Tsujimura Propositions 1.2(ii),4.2; Hoshi-Mochizuki-Tsujimura Proposition 6.4
notes: A characteristic positive-genus finite cover is descended through H s(G_F); equal actual point sections lift to rational points and proper Jacobian injectivity separates them. No section-surjectivity assertion is used.

statement: For every n,m>=1 and zeta in mu_n, the cover w^n=z, u^m=1-zeta w has isomorphic G_F-fibres above zeta6 and its inverse.
notes: The equivariant bijection is w'=zeta^-2 w^-1 and u'=lambda_w u with lambda_w^m=-(zeta w)^-1. All roots used are in F. Exact program checks all n,m<=12 and all zeta in mu_n: 7800 fibre-branch checks. The algebraic identity proves the result for all n,m.

statement: A connected finite etale cover of degree81 separates the full point sections at zeta6 and zeta6^-1 over Q(mu_infty).
depends_on: exact Fermat-cubic group law; Milne Elliptic Curves II.6.3-6.4,V.8.1,V.8.3
notes: The cover is R -> 3R+P -> w^3 on w^3+v^3=1, P=(zeta18,zeta18^-1). Exact Q(zeta18) calculations give orders1,3 over zeta6 and order9 for all differences over its inverse. Frobenius7 and complex conjugation prove E(F)[3^infty] is killed by9, so the latter fibre has no F-point while the former has one. The fibre permutation representation gives the required implication to full sections. Only the elementary abelianness of cyclotomic extensions is used.

statement: Cyclotomic-base Conjecture A is false: the smooth projective curve t^6+2y^3+4=0 over Q(mu_infty) has genus4, no rational point, and a continuous arithmetic section; the example persists over pure transcendental extensions.
depends_on: Clark Theorem1; Milne Class Field Theory VII.7.2,III.2.1,VIII.4.2,II.1.30; finite lifting proof given here
depends_on_doubtful_reading: scan62: tous nos beaux enonces does not specify a restricted surviving family
notes: The proper map to X^3+2Y^3+4Z^3=0 and a 2-adic valuation obstruction prove absence of points. Brauer vanishing over every finite extension implies H2 vanishing; a Frattini-kernel argument solves finite embedding problems and constructs compatible continuous sections. This is an explicit proof of section existence, with no section conjecture or freeness conjecture assumed.

statement: Manuscript Theorem2 holds for finitely generated extensions of F=K(mu_infty): F-embeddings with the same outer continuous Galois homomorphism are equal.
manuscript_passages: section 1; p.10; scan 22 | section 3; p.30; scan 62
depends_on_doubtful_reading: scan22: groupoid homomorphisms over the base groupoid and the explicit inner ambiguity
notes: The base-linear hypothesis is explicit. Kummer pullbacks force all f(a)/g(a) to be roots of unity; the comparisons for a,a+1,a+i in a complex embedding prove equality. No assertion about unrelated Q-linear coefficient actions is substituted.

statement: Theorem3 does not extend to cyclotomic bases: 1 and zeta6 on Gm have identical full section classes. The precise semiabelian replacement is equality modulo the intersection of all multiples of the rational-point group.
manuscript_passages: section 1; p.15; scan 32 | section 3; p.30; scan 62
depends_on_doubtful_reading: none; no marginal scope change is needed for the Gm counterexample
notes: The counterexample persists after every extension of F. The distinction between full and abelianized section claims is implemented by the actual quotient map; D2 proves full injectivity for hyperbolic curves.

statement: Theorem1's centralizers of open subgroups vanish for absolute Galois groups of finitely generated extensions of F and for their geometric absolute Galois groups.
manuscript_passages: section 1; pp.6-7; scans 13-15 | section 3; p.30; scan 62
depends_on_doubtful_reading: scans14-15: rank qualification and limit issues treated in B5,B12
notes: Hilbertianity and B12 cover every transcendence degree; the geometric group in transcendence degree zero is trivial. No cofinal-system assertion is assumed.

statement: The hyperbolic Proposition54 and point/cusp centralizer precisions persist over F and finitely generated extensions; type(0,2) still refutes the unqualified packet assertion, and Conjecture A is false by D5.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: scan54 centralizer versus normalizer is resolved by the explicit action map in C1
notes: The finite-extension AVKF and Tate-module hypotheses are checked before applying the already proved covering arguments. The first packet assertion's type(0,2) exception is retained in its own requirement row.

statement: Two hyperbolic curves over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field have isomorphic universal pro-curves exactly when they admit a connected common finite etale cover; completion is canonical and functorial for semilinear isomorphisms.
notes: Finite-presentation descent of both inverse maps, Zariski's main theorem, properness of the composite and the derivative check prove the common-cover direction. The fixed-point set is explicitly the inverse limit of compatible geometric points of compactifications; generic scheme points are not counted.

statement: An action on a Poincare pro-curve with open stabilizers on every rational function descends over an open normal Galois subgroup to any chosen finite level and comes from a continuous arithmetic section. The families of continuous B' and B over all finite extensions are equivalent.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: scan59: proposed conv. simple-discrete; scan63: no normalization assumed
notes: The proof intersects stabilizers of field generators and model coefficients, takes a normal core, and identifies the automorphism group with E_U. At one base the exact implications are {B_L for all finite L/K} => continuous B'_K => B_K. The stronger fixed-base quantifier is not asserted. D5 refutes the continuous existence assertion over the cyclotomic base.

statement: For a proper hyperbolic curve over Qbar (or an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field embedded in C), Aut of the universal pro-curve is the Belyaev completion of its uniformizing commensurator, profinite in the nonarithmetic case and locally compact noncompact in the arithmetic case.
notes: The compact genus>=2 hypothesis of the opened solenoid theorem is retained. The analytic/algebraic comparison and descent of finite-cover isomorphisms are supplied. The arithmeticity index criterion is explicitly recorded in the opened source's Introduction p3 and Corollary11 discussion. Affine curves are not included in this result.

statement: D(e) remains unfinished for discontinuous actions normalizing no finite-level deck group and for the affine commensurator-completion description; the exact abstract-cocycle construction problem is stated for the U03 Poincare curve over Qbar.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: scan63 explicitly omits an assumption that the action normalizes a deck group
notes: Partly settled: common covers, completion and continuous descent are proved. The outstanding task is to construct or exclude a function a_g in Aut_Qbar(U~) with a_gh=a_g rho0(g)a_h rho0(g)^-1 and no invariant profinite deck group. No speculative modular-translation construction is asserted. The unrestricted B' assertion is written explicitly as uniqueness and existence of a compatible G_Q^circ-fixed geometric point.

statement: For good marked reduction over a finite extension K/Qp, the prime-to-p geometric quotient is entirely fixed by G_{K(mu_infty)} for integral point sections and integral tangents. A cusp twist fixes the whole quotient exactly when all prime-to-p valuation components vanish, and otherwise fixes exactly cusp inertia.
depends_on: SGA1 XIII.2.9-2.11; Stacks Tag0C0R; Nakamura Lemmas(2.1.2),(2.1.4); A2
manuscript_passages: section 3; pp.27,30; scans 55-56,62; local-field extension requested in E(d)
notes: Good reduction means smooth proper compactification with finite etale boundary; the rational point must be integral and avoid the boundary on reduction. The proof uses the actual section action, unramified pointed specialization, Kummer valuation components and Nakamura's full-class theorem for all prime-to-p finite groups. Equation(E.4) computes every cuspidal twist under these hypotheses.

statement: The full-group and bad-marked-reduction parts of E(d) remain unfinished; the precise nonabelian H1 obstruction to lifting a fixed element from the prime-to-p quotient is proved.
manuscript_passages: section 3; pp.27,30; scans 55-56,62; local-field extension requested in E(d)
notes: The only general implication proved is q(pi^Delta) subseteq (pi^(p'))^Delta. A quotient-fixed lift h has obstruction d_sigma=h^-1 sigma(h) in H1(Delta,ker q). Smallest full-group instance retained: U03/Q5, point2 or integral tangent0. Bad-marked instance: P1 minus{0,1,5,infinity}/Q5, point2; both full and prime-to5 groups remain uncomputed. Mochizuki's arithmetic-isomorphism/cusp-preservation theorem is quoted with its actual hypotheses and is not substituted for this calculation.
